source_text: Ὃς ἂν οὑν ἐλθὼν διδάξῃ ὑμᾶς ταῦτα πάντα τὰ προειρημένα, δέξασθε αὐτόν: ἐὰν δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ διδάσκων στραφεὶς διδάσκῃ ἄλλην διδαχὴν εἰς τὸ καταλῦσαι, μὴ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε: εἰς δὲ τὸ προσθεῖναι δικαιοσύνην καὶ γνῶσιν κυρίου, δέξασθε αὐτὸν ὡς κύριον. Περὶ δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, κατὰ τὸ δόγμα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὕτω ποιήσατε. πᾶς δὲ ἀπόστολος ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς δεχθήτω ὡς κύριος: οὐ μενεῖ δὲ εἰ μὴ ἡμέραν μίαν: ἐὰν δὲ ᾖ χρεία, καὶ τὴν ἄλλην: τρεῖς δὲ ἐὰν μείνῃ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν. ἐξερχόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀπόστολος μηδὲν λαμβανέτω εἰ μὴ ἄρτον, ἕως οὖ αὐλισθῇ: ἐὰν δὲ ἀργύριον αἰτῇ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. Καὶ πάντα προφήτην λαλοῦντα ἐν πνεύματι οὐ πειράσετε οὐδὲ διακρινεῖτε: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται. οὐ πᾶς δὲ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν πνεύματι προφήτης ἐστίν, ἀλλ’ ἐὰν ἔχῃ τοὺς τρόπους κυρίου. ἀπὸ οὖν τῶν τρόπων γνωσθήσεται ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης καὶ ὁ προφήτης. καὶ πᾶς προφήτης ὁρίζων τράπεζαν ἐν πνεύματι οὐ φάγεται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, εἰ δὲ μήγε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης διδάσκων τὴν ἀλήθειαν, εἰ ἃ διδάσκει οὐ ποιεῖ. ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης δεδοκιμασμένος, ἀληθινός, ποιῶν εἰς μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας, μὴ διδάσκων δὲ ποιεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, οὐ κριθήσεται ἐφ̓ ὑμῶν: μετὰ θεοῦ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν κρίσιν: ὡσαύτως γὰρ ἐποίησαν καὶ οἱ ἀρχαῖοι προφῆται. ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ ἐν πνεύματι: δός μοι ἀργύρια ἢ ἕτερά τινα, οὐκ ἀκούσεσθε αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ περὶ ἄλλων ὑστερούντων εἴπῃ δοῦναι, μηδεὶς αὐτὸν κρινέτω.
pass_a_gloss: Whoever comes and teaches you all these things previously mentioned, receive him; but if he himself, the teacher, turns and teaches another teaching to destroy, do not listen to him; but to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord. Now concerning the apostles and prophets, do thus according to the doctrine of the gospel. Every apostle coming to you, let him be received as the Lord; he will not stay except one day; but if there is need, also the next; but if he stays three, he is a false prophet. The apostle coming out must not take anything except bread, until he is lodged; but if he asks for money, he is a false prophet. And every prophet speaking in the Spirit, you will not test nor discern; for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Not everyone speaking in the Spirit is a prophet, but if he has the ways of the Lord. Therefore, the false prophet and the prophet will be known from their ways. And every prophet who ordains a table in the Spirit will not eat from it, unless he is indeed a false prophet. Every prophet teaching the truth, if he does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. Every approved prophet, true, doing for the mystery of the church's worldly things, but not teaching to do what he himself does, will not be judged by you; for he has his judgment with God; for the ancient prophets did likewise. But whoever says in the Spirit: give me money or something else, you will not listen to him; but if he says to give to others who are in need, let no one judge him.

choices.why: comparing the apostle's reception to the Lord's

pass_b_english: Receive anyone who comes to teach you all the things I have just mentioned. But if the teacher himself turns and teaches a different doctrine to destroy, do not listen to him. However, receive him as the Lord if he teaches to add to your righteousness and knowledge of the Lord. Now, regarding the apostles and prophets, do this according to the gospel's teaching. Let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord. He should not stay longer than one day, unless there is a need, in which case he may stay the next. But if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. An apostle who goes out must not take anything except bread until he is lodged. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet. You must not test or judge every prophet who speaks in the Spirit, for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he has the ways of the Lord. Therefore, the false prophet and the true prophet will be known by their ways. And every prophet who sets a table in the Spirit will not eat from it unless he is indeed a false prophet. Every prophet who teaches the truth but does not practice what he teaches is a false prophet. An approved prophet, who is true and does things for the mystery of the church, will not be judged by you if he does not teach what he does, for he has his judgment with God, just as the ancient prophets did. But if anyone says in the Spirit, 'Give me money or something else,' you will not listen to him. However, if he says to give to others who are in need, let no one judge him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the sin that is forgiven and the sin that is not, the specific conditions for receiving apostles and prophets, and the criteria for identifying false prophets. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
